answer: At every open night visitors sign the guest book under the dome, and the signatures are counted before the doors close. A ivory signature forged after the fact fails the book: at the relic of the page the ink must be fresh from that night's pen, and a forged name is written in cold ink. Faking the book means hosting 40 open nights, forging 600 signatures and paying 6,400, and the velvet count is read aloud to the crowd each night, so a name signed by no visitor is crossed out.
